reason: VALUE/TRANSFER lens. The idea survives narrowly, with a smaller gain than claimed and two corrections. (1) Not a node-count artefact: nodes are untouched, so the node multiplier term is exactly 0. (2) Sign on unseen data: the idea's '12x enrichment' (24% of forks vs 2% of GT) says nothing about value, because 96-100% of forks are ignored by the metric (x138 dummies: 0/62 evaluable; old base on the same 4 clips: 0/54). I recomputed the rule on an independent labelled set: the old-base exp39 final graph on ALL 199 train clips (div_audit9.json, approximate labels; t+1 valley by the same recipe, scratchpad fb_oldbase_valley.json). The cell (s<=5 um, v>=0.95) holds 68 forks: 3 evaluable FP, 0 TP, 65 free. The only close TP fork (6bba_4f99ce20 t94, 4.87 um) has valley 0.60 and is spared. The rule is training-free and its thresholds come from GT, so there is no in-sample leak. (3) Ceiling from the metric (score = adj_edge + 0.1*div_J): public div_J ~0.36 (probe 26), S_div ~25-30 public / ~70 private. One vetoed FP = +0.0013 public / +0.0005 private; one lost TP = -0.0036 / -0.0014 (break-even FP:TP 2.8). Expected dose: 0.015 evaluable cell-FP per clip at old-base density; x138 has ~5x more cell forks (15 vs 3 on the same 4 dummy clips), so 0.015-0.075/clip gives 0.4-2.2 events on public (~29 clips) and 1.1-5.3 on private (~71). With a Laplace TP share (~1:4) this gives about +0.0005 public and +0.0005..+0.001 private, not the claimed +0.001 public. (4) Partly a closed line in disguise: on the x138 dummies the valley does not bind at all (15/15 forks with s<=5 have v>=0.95). There forkblob IS a post-hoc 5 um sister floor. The pre-link 5 um floor (B27b) was LB-probed: probe 18 = 0.946 vs 0.947, a tie 'mildly against on sign'; probe 25 bundle 0.946. It differs in that it is post-hoc (does not refill per-frame caps with other candidates) and the valley spares 2 of 5 close GT divisions, so it is not identical. Keep that probe as the prior, though, and do not read an LB tie as a failure or a +0.001 as a confirmation. (5) The test gate is wrong on edges: 'adj_edge unchanged by construction' is false. In 2 of the 3 old-base cell FPs the ADDED edge is the GT-successor edge TP and the ILP edge goes to an unmatched node, so dropping the added edge loses an edge TP. The cost is ~1/S_edge ~5e-5 per event (648 GT edges/clip), which is negligible, but the gate must allow it. (6) Power: the exp60 lab (56 clips) expects only ~1-4 evaluable cell events, so its FP:TP clause cannot confirm value; it can only catch TP harm.
fix: (a) Rewrite gate (1) of the test: pooled adj_edge change >= -0.0002 instead of 'unchanged'. Log per vetoed fork which edge was dropped, whether it was an edge TP/FP/ignored, and the fork's division label. (b) Pre-register in CONTEXT, before exp60 is read, the independent 199-clip old-base result (cell 3 FP / 0 TP / 65 free) as the sign evidence. Use exp60 as a HARM check only: pooled 0 TP vetoed, or <= 1 TP with >= 3 FP, plus the dose check (>= 10% of control forks in the cell). Drop the per-half div_J clause, which has no power at ~1-4 events. (c) State in the plan that on x138 forkblob ~= a post-hoc 5 um sister floor (valley non-binding on 15/15 dummy forks). Cite probe 18 (0.946 vs 0.947) as the prior. Accept K3 under R3 only as a guard (public >= K2 - 0.001), never as confirmation. (d) Keep the pre-registered s <= 5 um. Do NOT widen it to catch the 10 one-blob FPs at 5-10 um seen on the old base: that would be a post-hoc lab-tuned knob, and 5-7 um holds real divisions. (e) Keep it a separate env knob in K3 so that a K3 tie/drop can be reverted per rider in the finals build without a new probe. Ship it only if the lab harm check passes.
realistic_gain: Public +0.0005 central (range -0.0035..+0.003; P(<0) ~0.2-0.25; 0.4-2.2 expected evaluable events, so most likely invisible at the LB's 0.001 rounding). Private +0.0005..+0.001 (1-5 events, lower variance). Edge term ~ -0.0001 at worst. Node term 0. Worth a cheap rider only after the exp60 harm check; not worth a dedicated LB slot.
